A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.3 V is provided. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The stable passivation film formed by vinylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and vinylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The structure with the aluminum current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 60 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: molybdenum disulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid. Polysulfide dissolution from the molybdenum disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The active material is coated with a thin lithium phosphosulfide ion conductor layer so that the cathode can be used in a solid-state cell. The carbon nanotubes framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of molybdenum disulfide. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyacrylic acid. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 800 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. The molybdenum disulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with carbon nanotubes by ball milling.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising molybdenum disulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 2 stacked cells
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 3 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 600 to 750 degrees C. The gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte of 95% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 95%. The cell operates at 600 to 750 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 50 cycles. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the gadolinium-doped ceria cell.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 95% or more.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The LLZO and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. With the additive in an amount of 1 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which zinc is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% to suppress dendrites. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.3 V is provided. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The stable passivation film formed by lithium difluorophosphate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The 1.5 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium difluorophosphate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor having a porous tantalum anode body and a hybrid electrolyte
abstract: A hybrid capacitor combining a conductive polymer layer and an electrolytic solution is described. The polystyrene sulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 150 degrees C storage. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the tantalum anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. A capacitance of 220 microfarads is obtained in a case size of 7.3 mm by 4.3 mm. The tantalum anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor. A solid electrolyte of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) layer to serve as the cathode lead-out.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising: anodizing a porous tantalum anode body to form a dielectric oxide film; impregnating the anode body with a dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles having a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm; drying the dispersion to form a conductive polymer layer; and forming a carbon layer and a silver layer on the conductive polymer layer.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 94%. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The method gives reproducible densification and improved ionic conductivity at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 91% or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using tetrahydrofuran
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: Disclosed is a semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of polycarbonate holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The polymer matrix is polycarbonate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The polycarbonate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polycarbonate; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the content of LiI is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability and electrochemical window of the solid-state lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: Described is a combination of lithium bis(oxalato)borate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The 1.5 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 90% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The capacity retention of 90% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium bis(oxalato)borate. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.5 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium bis(oxalato)borate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

assignee_raw: CORAST INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
assignee_db_group: CORAST INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY INDUSTRY ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li2ZrO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

assignee_raw: UNIVERSITY OF BELUNEA INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
assignee_db_group: UNIVERSITY OF BELUNEA INDUSTRY ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyethylene oxide chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: An amperometric sensor in which hydrogen is pumped through a diffusion barrier by an oxide ion conducting ceramic is provided. A lithium carbonate auxiliary electrode may be used for detecting carbon dioxide at 400 degrees C. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the gold sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The protective layer improves the durability of the NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate sensor in an exhaust gas. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 400 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode of sodium nitrite makes the sensor selective to hydrogen against interfering gases. The sensing electrode comprises gold and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: titanium disulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a titanium disulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. The cathode with a loading of 4 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The composite shows a capacity of 1400 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The confinement of titanium disulfide in the porous carbon suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the titanium disulfide cathode.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing titanium disulfide with porous carbon; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the titanium disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Potentiometric ammonia sensor having an auxiliary electrode of sodium carbonate
abstract: This disclosure concerns a multilayer ceramic sensor element produced by co-firing green sheets of zirconia and alumina. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of ammonia concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The ammonia sensor can be used for combustion control and emission monitoring at 300 degrees C. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 300 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising platinum, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of ammonia.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The anode support contains nickel oxide and scandia-stabilized zirconia in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 650 to 800 degrees C. The cell operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a power density of 1.2 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 200 cycles. The solid electrolyte layer of scandia-stabilized zirconia conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The reversible cell with a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 98%.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 650 to 800 degrees C.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: A reversible solid oxide cell with a 15 micrometer electrolyte operable in fuel cell mode and electrolysis mode at 650 to 800 degrees C is described. The lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte of 96% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 650 to 800 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 15 micrometers. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 650 to 800 degrees C. The solid electrolyte of lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite is a dense ceramic of 96% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. A power density of 1.2 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 650 to 800 degrees C operating range.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 15 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Planar solid oxide fuel cell stack with metal interconnects and a glass sealant
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The anode support contains nickel oxide and samarium-doped ceria in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers and a relative density of 95%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 700 to 850 degrees C. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the samarium-doped ceria electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The solid electrolyte layer of samarium-doped ceria conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The cell can be operated at 700 to 850 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The samarium-doped ceria electrolyte of 95% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 700 to 850 degrees C.

assignee_raw: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Potentiometric ammonia sensor having an auxiliary electrode of sodium carbonate
abstract: An amperometric sensor in which ammonia is pumped through a diffusion barrier by an oxide ion conducting ceramic is provided. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 700 degrees C. The limiting current is proportional to the ammonia concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The ammonia sensor can be used for combustion control and emission monitoring at 700 degrees C. The ceramic is sodium beta-alumina and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 700 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising sodium beta-alumina, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

assignee_raw: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
assignee_db_group: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor with a conductive polymer solid electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a solid electrolytic capacitor element whose leakage current is reduced by a repair step of the dielectric film. The capacitor withstands 150 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. The capacitor rated at 6.3 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the tantalum anode.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles doped with p-toluenesulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: Described is a combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The capacity retention of 90% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. The combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. With 3 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 90% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive lithium difluorophosphate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 90% with the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium difluorophosphate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% to suppress dendrites. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. The magnesium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

title: aluminum solid electrolytic capacitor having a low equivalent series resistance
abstract: A hybrid capacitor combining a conductive polymer layer and an electrolytic solution is described. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. The capacitor rated at 10 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The equivalent series resistance is 20 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the aluminum anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. The solid electrolyte is the conductive polymer layer that serves as the true cathode of the capacitor. The poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 20 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising: anodizing a porous aluminum anode body to form a dielectric oxide film; impregnating the anode body with a dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles having a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm; drying the dispersion to form a conductive polymer layer; and forming a carbon layer and a silver layer on the conductive polymer layer.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 89% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material. The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with silica nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The 30 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 30 micrometers. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 40 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

title: Planar solid oxide fuel cell stack with metal interconnects and a glass sealant
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 8 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers and a relative density of 96%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 700 to 850 degrees C. The solid electrolyte of scandia-stabilized zirconia is a dense ceramic of 96% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The cell can be operated at 700 to 850 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 700 to 850 degrees C. The cathode comprises barium strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 96% or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.5 V. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 3 wt% of vinylene carbonate is also described. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The additive vinylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. With 3 wt% of vinylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 90% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium secondary battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor with a conductive polymer solid electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and a capacitor using the dispersion are provided. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the aluminum capacitor. The capacitor has a capacitance of 220 microfarads, a rated voltage of 6.3 V, and an equivalent series resistance of 10 milliohms at 100 kHz. The aluminum anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor comprising a plurality of capacitor elements stacked and electrically connected in parallel, each capacitor element comprising a aluminum anode body, a dielectric layer, and a conductive polymer layer, and a resin encapsulation, wherein the capacitor has a rated voltage of 6.3 V.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: Provided is an oxygen-ion conducting ceramic electrolyte for a fuel cell that operates at 700 to 850 degrees C with a lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 700 to 850 degrees C. The gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte of 97% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the gadolinium-doped ceria cell. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 8 micrometers. A 8 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. A power density of 1.5 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 700 to 850 degrees C operating range.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising gadolinium-doped ceria; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and capacitor using the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a aluminum solid electrolytic capacitor with a low equivalent series resistance and a high rated voltage. The capacitor rated at 16 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. A solid electrolyte of polypyrrole replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 150 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the polypyrrole layer to serve as the cathode lead-out. The capacitor has a capacitance of 47 microfarads, a rated voltage of 16 V, and an equivalent series resistance of 15 milliohms at 100 kHz.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor comprising a plurality of capacitor elements stacked and electrically connected in parallel, each capacitor element comprising a aluminum anode body, a dielectric layer, and a conductive polymer layer, and a resin encapsulation, wherein the capacitor has a rated voltage of 16 V.

title: Electrochemical gas sensor with a NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate solid electrolyte for detecting carbon dioxide
abstract: Described is a thick film gas sensor whose sensing electrode is printed on a ceramic ion conductor. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux.
