title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The current collector of nickel-plated copper is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polycarbonate and lithium hexafluorophosphate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of polycarbonate holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. The anion is covalently bonded to the polycarbonate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polycarbonate; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, fluoroethylene carbonate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. The additive vinylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 85% of its capacity after 300 cycles. The 1.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and vinylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 20 micrometers or less.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: Described is a combination of lithium bis(oxalato)borate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium bis(oxalato)borate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 100 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The stable passivation film formed by lithium bis(oxalato)borate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The 1.0 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.0 M and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 500 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. A lithium battery pack comprising 8 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1100 degrees C, and the resulting density is 97%. The resulting LLTO and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12 and LiF present at grain boundaries. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 10 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. The cathode comprises barium strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The reversible cell with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 700 to 850 degrees C. The barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 700 to 850 degrees C. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers and a relative density of 97%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 700 to 850 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 97% or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing 1,3-propane sultone as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a combination of 1,3-propane sultone and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The stable passivation film formed by 1,3-propane sultone suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The cell retains 92% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 700 to 850 degrees C. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 700 to 850 degrees C. The thin 10 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.5 W/cm2. The cell may also be combined with a lithium battery in a hybrid power system operating at 700 to 850 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 10 micrometers. The lanthanum strontium manganite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 700 to 850 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 700 to 850 degrees C.

title: Amperometric ammonia sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 700 degrees C. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 700 degrees C. The ceramic is yttria-stabilized zirconia and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 700 degrees C. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The sensor detects ammonia with high selectivity and a response time of 10 seconds. The limiting current is proportional to the ammonia concentration from 0.1% to 20%.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising gold, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of ammonia.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell and a sensing cell on a zirconia substrate
abstract: Described is a thick film gas sensor whose sensing electrode is printed on a ceramic ion conductor. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The sensor shows a response time of 10 seconds to a step change of sulfur dioxide concentration at 400 degrees C. The sulfur dioxide sensor can be used for combustion control and emission monitoring at 400 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode comprises lithium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The multilayer structure with the sodium beta-alumina ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the platinum sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting sulfur dioxide, comprising: a ceramic body comprising sodium beta-alumina; a sensing electrode comprising platinum disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 400 degrees C.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. The anode support contains nickel oxide and scandia-stabilized zirconia in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The scandia-stabilized zirconia solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. The cell can be operated at 650 to 800 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The reversible cell with a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The cell operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a power density of 1.0 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 200 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 650 to 800 degrees C.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 500 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Surface mount solid electrolytic capacitor and method of reducing leakage current
abstract: This disclosure concerns a surface mount capacitor with a conductive polymer cathode and a lead frame. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the polypyrrole layer to serve as the cathode lead-out. The equivalent series resistance is 15 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The dispersion of polypyrrole gives a uniform polymer layer and a high capacitance appearance rate for the 220 microfarad rating. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. The capacitor rated at 6.3 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor comprising a plurality of capacitor elements stacked and electrically connected in parallel, each capacitor element comprising a niobium anode body, a dielectric layer, and a conductive polymer layer, and a resin encapsulation, wherein the capacitor has a rated voltage of 6.3 V.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor element with a poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) layer and a carbon cathode layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method for forming a conductive polymer layer by impregnating a dielectric-coated anode body with a dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles. The 100 microfarad capacitor smooths the output of a lithium battery converter. The aluminum capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed. The solid electrolyte layer covers the dielectric oxide film inside the pores of the anode body. A capacitance of 100 microfarads is obtained in a case size of 7.3 mm by 4.3 mm. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 105 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. The poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 5 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising: anodizing a porous aluminum anode body to form a dielectric oxide film; impregnating the anode body with a dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles having a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm; drying the dispersion to form a conductive polymer layer; and forming a carbon layer and a silver layer on the conductive polymer layer.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 15 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 15 micrometers. The cell may also be combined with a lithium battery in a hybrid power system operating at 700 to 850 degrees C. The yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 96% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a relative density of 96%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 700 to 850 degrees C. The anode support contains nickel oxide and yttria-stabilized zirconia in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 15 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

assignee_db_group: DALANE UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 500 to 650 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: Disclosed is a solid oxide fuel cell in which a thin scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte is co-sintered with an anode support to lower the ohmic resistance of the cell. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 500 to 650 degrees C. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the scandia-stabilized zirconia cell. The cell can be operated at 500 to 650 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. A 15 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 15 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 500 to 650 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and production method thereof
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: A reversible solid oxide cell with a 10 micrometer electrolyte operable in fuel cell mode and electrolysis mode at 600 to 750 degrees C is described. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 96%. The solid electrolyte of yttria-stabilized zirconia is a dense ceramic of 96% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 10 micrometers. The barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 600 to 750 degrees C. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers and a relative density of 96%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 600 to 750 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises nickel sulfide impregnated in carbon nanotubes and a carbon coating on the composite. The cathode with a loading of 4 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The nickel sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 800 mAh/g and retains 85% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the nickel sulfide cathode. The carbon coating on the nickel sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. A lithium-sulfur battery with the nickel sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing nickel sulfide with carbon nanotubes; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the nickel sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising an Ag-C inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more.

title: Mixed potential type oxygen sensor and method of manufacturing the sensing electrode
abstract: An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting oxygen comprises a lanthanum fluoride ceramic, a sensing electrode comprising platinum, and a reference electrode exposed to a reference gas. The platinum electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 400 degrees C. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The limiting current is proportional to the oxygen concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The sensor detects oxygen with high selectivity and a response time of 5 seconds. The auxiliary electrode comprises sodium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising sodium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects oxygen.

title: Planar solid oxide fuel cell stack with metal interconnects and a glass sealant
abstract: Disclosed is a solid oxide fuel cell in which a thin scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte is co-sintered with an anode support to lower the ohmic resistance of the cell. The cell operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a power density of 1.2 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 200 cycles. The thin 15 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.2 W/cm2. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 15 micrometers. The cell can be operated at 650 to 800 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The stack of 200 cells can be paired with a lithium battery for load leveling. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 650 to 800 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The structure with the nickel-plated copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. With 3 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.3 V. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 500 cycles is 92% with the electrolyte. With 0.5 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 92% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte
abstract: A solid oxide fuel cell includes a porous nickel-cermet anode support, a dense electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria with a thickness of 15 micrometers or less, a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria, and a perovskite cathode. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The samarium-doped ceria solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode at 700 to 850 degrees C. The thin 15 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 0.8 W/cm2. The cell operates at 700 to 850 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 700 to 850 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, fluoroethylene carbonate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: Conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and capacitor using the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for forming a conductive polymer layer by impregnating a dielectric-coated anode body with a dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the niobium anode. A capacitance of 330 microfarads is obtained in a case size of 7.3 mm by 4.3 mm. The niobium capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the niobium capacitor. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. The poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) is doped with polystyrene sulfonate and has a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm in the dispersion.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising: anodizing a porous niobium anode body to form a dielectric oxide film; impregnating the anode body with a dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles having a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm; drying the dispersion to form a conductive polymer layer; and forming a carbon layer and a silver layer on the conductive polymer layer.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte
abstract: A solid oxide fuel cell includes a porous nickel-cermet anode support, a dense electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia with a thickness of 15 micrometers or less, a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria, and a perovskite cathode. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 700 to 850 degrees C. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the scandia-stabilized zirconia cell. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 700 to 850 degrees C. The scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 95% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. A 15 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 15 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 700 to 850 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. A solid electrolyte sheet of 30 micrometers is used as the separator. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Composite cathode comprising sulfur and graphene and lithium secondary battery
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. The sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 80% at 25 degrees C. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The sulfur is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The sulfur particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling. A lithium-sulfur battery with the sulfur cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The graphene framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of sulfur.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; sulfur impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a multilayer ceramic sensor element produced by co-firing green sheets of zirconia and alumina. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover. The multilayer structure with the gadolinium-doped ceria ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 300 degrees C. The protective layer improves the durability of the gadolinium-doped ceria sensor in an exhaust gas. The ceramic is gadolinium-doped ceria and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 300 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting ammonia, comprising: a ceramic body comprising gadolinium-doped ceria; a sensing electrode comprising platinum disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 300 degrees C.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ceramic ion conductor in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Electrochemical gas sensor with a lanthanum fluoride solid electrolyte for detecting hydrogen
abstract: Described is a thick film gas sensor whose sensing electrode is printed on a ceramic ion conductor. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the platinum sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 300 degrees C. The protective layer improves the durability of the lanthanum fluoride sensor in an exhaust gas. The sensor shows a response time of 2 seconds to a step change of hydrogen concentration at 300 degrees C. The sensor operating at 300 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for hydrogen.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising platinum, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of hydrogen.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, lithium difluorophosphate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. With 3 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive lithium difluorophosphate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 500 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 100 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing.
