The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive in an amount of 0.5 wt%. With 0.5 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 85% with the electrolyte. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The 1.0 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte
abstract: A reversible solid oxide cell with a 3 micrometer electrolyte operable in fuel cell mode and electrolysis mode at 500 to 650 degrees C is described. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. A power density of 1.0 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 500 to 650 degrees C operating range. The cell can be operated at 500 to 650 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 95%. The yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 95% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 3 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The LLZO, LLTO, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 5 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite cell. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 500 to 650 degrees C. A power density of 0.8 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 500 to 650 degrees C operating range. The lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte of 98% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. A 5 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing. The warm isostatic pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor element with a poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) layer and a carbon cathode layer
abstract: A solid electrolytic capacitor includes a porous niobium anode body, a dielectric oxide film formed on the anode body, a conductive polymer layer comprising poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) doped with naphthalenesulfonate, a carbon layer, and a silver layer. The equivalent series resistance is 15 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The anode body is a sintered pellet of niobium powder having a specific charge of 50,000 to 150,000 microfarad volts per gram. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. The niobium anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 105 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles doped with naphthalenesulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 5.5 mS/cm. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the content of LiI is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Composite cathode comprising molybdenum disulfide and carbon nanotubes and lithium secondary battery
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, carbon nanotubes, and polyvinylidene fluoride is described. The molybdenum disulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with carbon nanotubes by ball milling. A separator coated with carbon nanotubes traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 2 mg/cm2. The initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the molybdenum disulfide cathode. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 80% at 25 degrees C. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising molybdenum disulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Solid oxide electrolysis cell and reversible fuel cell having a thin dense electrolyte
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 10 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 650 to 800 degrees C. A power density of 1.5 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 650 to 800 degrees C operating range. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite cell. The lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 98%. The stack shows stable operation over 200 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 650 to 800 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 650 to 800 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: Provided is an oxygen-ion conducting ceramic electrolyte for a fuel cell that operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 650 to 800 degrees C. The cell can be operated at 650 to 800 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The solid electrolyte of samarium-doped ceria is a dense ceramic of 98% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the samarium-doped ceria electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The samarium-doped ceria electrolyte of 98% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 650 to 800 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 650 to 800 degrees C.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with aluminum and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The resulting Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Sintering at 1200 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 93% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate and a film-forming additive
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate is added in an amount of 2 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The cell retains 85% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate at 1.2 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.5 V. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. A separator coated with graphene traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The initial capacity of 600 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The capacity retention after 200 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The sulfur is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the sulfur cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The sulfur cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising sulfur, graphene, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the sulfur is 2 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Composite cathode comprising lithium sulfide and graphene and lithium secondary battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium sulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The cathode with a loading of 5 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 85% at 25 degrees C. A lithium-sulfur battery with the lithium sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising lithium sulfide, graphene, and polyvinylidene fluoride, wherein a loading of the lithium sulfide is 5 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin samarium-doped ceria electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A solid oxide fuel cell includes a porous nickel-cermet anode support, a dense electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria with a thickness of 5 micrometers or less, a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria, and a perovskite cathode. A power density of 1.0 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 600 to 750 degrees C operating range. The reversible cell with a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the samarium-doped ceria electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The anode support contains nickel oxide and samarium-doped ceria in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 600 to 750 degrees C.

title: Mixed potential type ammonia sensor and method of manufacturing the sensing electrode
abstract: An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting ammonia comprises a gadolinium-doped ceria ceramic, a sensing electrode comprising gold, and a reference electrode exposed to a reference gas. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 400 degrees C. The sensing electrode comprises gold and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the gold sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 400 degrees C. The protective layer improves the durability of the gadolinium-doped ceria sensor in an exhaust gas.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising gold, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of ammonia.

title: Solid oxide electrolysis cell and reversible fuel cell having a thin dense electrolyte
abstract: A solid oxide fuel cell includes a porous nickel-cermet anode support, a dense electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia with a thickness of 10 micrometers or less, a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria, and a perovskite cathode. The cell can be operated at 700 to 850 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The solid electrolyte of scandia-stabilized zirconia is a dense ceramic of 97% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. A power density of 1.2 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 700 to 850 degrees C operating range. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 97%. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 97% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 700 to 850 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 8 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. The solid electrolyte of scandia-stabilized zirconia is a dense ceramic of 96% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 700 to 850 degrees C. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 700 to 850 degrees C. A power density of 1.0 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 700 to 850 degrees C operating range. The cell can be operated at 700 to 850 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 96%.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 96% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is a combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. With 1 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The cold isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyethylene oxide matrix, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and an ionic liquid as a plasticizer. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyethylene oxide chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 30 micrometers or less.

title: niobium solid electrolytic capacitor having a low equivalent series resistance
abstract: A solid electrolytic capacitor includes a porous niobium anode body, a dielectric oxide film formed on the anode body, a conductive polymer layer comprising polyaniline doped with polystyrene sulfonate, a carbon layer, and a silver layer. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. The anode body is a sintered pellet of niobium powder having a specific charge of 50,000 to 150,000 microfarad volts per gram. The polyaniline layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 20 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide. The equivalent series resistance is 20 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The solid electrolyte layer covers the dielectric oxide film inside the pores of the anode body. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the niobium anode.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising: anodizing a porous niobium anode body to form a dielectric oxide film; impregnating the anode body with a dispersion of polyaniline particles having a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm; drying the dispersion to form a conductive polymer layer; and forming a carbon layer and a silver layer on the conductive polymer layer.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for a lithium secondary battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, lithium difluorophosphate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The 1.5 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The additive lithium difluorophosphate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyethylene oxide matrix. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 60 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell and a sensing cell on a zirconia substrate
abstract: An amperometric sensor in which carbon dioxide is pumped through a diffusion barrier by an oxide ion conducting ceramic is provided. The solid electrolyte of sodium beta-alumina conducts ions between the sensing electrode and the reference electrode. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to carbon dioxide against interfering gases. The ceramic is sodium beta-alumina and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 500 degrees C. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 500 degrees C. The limiting current is proportional to the carbon dioxide concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The sensing electrode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting carbon dioxide, comprising: a ceramic body comprising sodium beta-alumina; a sensing electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 500 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a lithium sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. A separator coated with graphene traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. A lithium-sulfur battery with the lithium sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% at 25 degrees C. The lithium sulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing lithium sulfide with graphene; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the lithium sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The solid electrolyte layer of samarium-doped ceria conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The thin 3 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 0.8 W/cm2. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the samarium-doped ceria electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The stack of 100 cells can be paired with a lithium battery for load leveling. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 500 to 650 degrees C. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 3 micrometers and a relative density of 96%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 500 to 650 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising samarium-doped ceria, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 3 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar aluminum current collectors. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The electrode mixture of the solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte
abstract: A reversible solid oxide cell with a 15 micrometer electrolyte operable in fuel cell mode and electrolysis mode at 600 to 750 degrees C is described. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 15 micrometers. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 600 to 750 degrees C. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. The reversible cell with a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. A 15 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 600 to 750 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate dissolved in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive in an amount of 2 wt%. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The combination of lithium bis(oxalato)borate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate is added in an amount of 2 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Multilayer ceramic gas sensor element and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a thick film gas sensor whose sensing electrode is printed on a ceramic ion conductor. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 500 degrees C. The lanthanum strontium manganite electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 500 degrees C. The protective layer improves the durability of the lanthanum fluoride sensor in an exhaust gas. The sensing electrode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of ammonia concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising lanthanum fluoride, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 50 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% over 100 cycles. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing vinylene carbonate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, vinylene carbonate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 92% of its capacity after 300 cycles. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 300 cycles is 92% with the electrolyte. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive vinylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The stable passivation film formed by vinylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising vinylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing 1,3-propane sultone as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The capacity retention of 88% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without 1,3-propane sultone. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising 1,3-propane sultone, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyacrylonitrile and lithium hexafluorophosphate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 30 micrometers or less.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing 1,3-propane sultone as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, 1,3-propane sultone, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The additive 1,3-propane sultone is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of 1,3-propane sultone is also described. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The combination of 1,3-propane sultone and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The capacity retention of 90% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without vinylene carbonate. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 300 cycles is 90% with the electrolyte. The stable passivation film formed by vinylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding vinylene carbonate in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing titania nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyethylene oxide chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 300 cycles is 88% with the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and capacitor using the same
abstract: Provided is a multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor in which capacitor elements are stacked and connected in parallel. The capacitor rated at 25 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The anode body is a sintered pellet of tantalum powder having a specific charge of 50,000 to 150,000 microfarad volts per gram. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) layer to serve as the cathode lead-out. The equivalent series resistance is 5 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The naphthalenesulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 105 degrees C storage.
first_claim: 1. A solid electrolytic capacitor comprising: an anode body comprising a porous sintered body of tantalum; a dielectric layer formed on a surface of the anode body; a conductive polymer layer disposed on the dielectric layer and comprising poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) doped with naphthalenesulfonate; and a cathode layer comprising carbon and silver disposed on the conductive polymer layer, wherein an equivalent series resistance of the capacitor at 100 kHz is 5 milliohms or less.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF material. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and method for producing the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity.
